title: Weyl-matrix evolution for bounded continuously differentiable Hermitian N-wave solutions with positive diagonal characteristic matrices on a semi-strip
author: Alexander L. Sakhnovich
work: Initial Value Problems for Integrable Systems on a Semi-Strip
source_version: Official SIGMA 12 (2016) article 001, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2016.001; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The proof controls a matrix fractional transformation uniformly in the unbounded spatial coordinate and proves its denominator remains invertible. It passes from finite-interval Weyl graphs to their half-line limits, then propagates the fractional evolution over the entire time strip through local contraction and analytic continuation. This spectral evolution argument exceeds writing the formal zero-curvature factorization.

source_check.note: The complete original Weyl evolution Theorem 4.1 and full author proof are retained for a uniformly bounded C1 Hermitian N-wave solution on the specified semi-strip. Exact fundamental-solution factorization, normalized triangular Weyl/finite-interval graph definitions and recovery are included as author-cited established background. The new positivity-based backward contraction, spatially uniform short-time property-J perturbation, graph limit, denominator invertibility, time-interval iteration and analytic continuation are supplied in full. The explicit uniform commutator/gap threshold and positive diagonal D-hat are retained; D-hat need not be ordered. No N-wave existence/full-rho uniqueness, ordered-D-hat initial-value theorem or dNLS quasi-analytic claim is selected. Existing approved human statement/proof/context/above-qualification decision copied from the frozen manifest and metadata; no new source or mathematical review.

proof_review.note: Complete4.1 author proof read, including fundamental-solution factorization, positivity-based backward time contraction, uniform short-time perturbation of property-J matrices, finite-spatial graph transformation and its limit, local denominator control, time interval iteration and analytic continuation. The normalized triangular Weyl construction and prior zero-curvature factorization are established cited background in2.2. No existence theorem, dNLS quasi-analytic claim, ordered-Dhat initial-value uniqueness4.2, or claim recovering an arbitrary diagonal of rho is selected.

original_metadata.statement_scope: D=diag(d1>...>dm>0), Dhat any positive diagonal matrix; rho=rho* uniformly bounded and C1 on x>=0,0<=t<a, satisfying N-wave1.8. R_t=(iz Dhat-[Dhat,rho(0,t)])R,R(0,z)=I. The normalized upper-triangular Weyl matrix for w_x=(izD-[D,rho])w evolves through the exact4.2 fractional graphs and4.3 column recovery, for Im z<-M with M above the explicit uniform commutator/gap threshold. Dhat need not be ordered. No existence or complete-rho uniqueness assertion.
